The main takeaway from our work is that

people with negative views of the self do not actively seek out critical feedback because they want it; they solicit it because they believe that they must have it in order to know what they are dealing with.

people with negative views of themselves are not necessarily motivated to seek out negative feedback about their self, and are not necessarily motivated by negative feedback about their selves to engage in behaviors that are self-defeating.

people who have a negative self-view (such as depressed people) do not actively seek out negative information, but they do tend to interpret neutral or positive information in a negative light, and this is a function of how they view their own self.
